back: The loose surface layer of weathered rock particles, organic matter, water and air in which plants grow.

front: Approximate make-up of a typical loam
back: About 45% mineral particles, 5% organic matter, 25% water, 25% air (by volume).
Texture: proportions of sand, silt and clay. Structure: how particles clump into crumbs, blocks or plates.
Sand: drains fast, holds little water and few nutrients, easy to work. Clay: drains slowly, holds water and nutrients, heavy and sticky.
In waterlogged soil, lack of oxygen reduces iron compounds, giving grey or blue-grey soil with rusty mottles: a gley soil.
Organic acids from litter combine with iron and aluminium and carry them down, leaving a bleached layer: podzolic soils.
Intense weathering and leaching in hot, wet climates leave iron and aluminium oxides: red latosols; hardened layers form laterite.

front: Soil horizons O, A, E, B, C, R
back: O litter; A topsoil; E eluviated (bleached); B subsoil (illuviation); C weathered parent material; R bedrock.
Water % = (fresh − dry) ÷ fresh × 100. Organic % = (dry − burnt) ÷ dry × 100.
